Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Australia's reply. The two umpires have made their way out to the middle as have the players of West Indies. David Warner and Ashton Agar will open the innings for Australia. West Indies are starting with spin in the form of Akeal Hosein. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Australia have a mountain to climb and they will have to make the most of the limited resources to get over the line here. As for West Indies, the batters have set the game up for them nicely and it is now up to the bowlers to back it up. Back in a bit for the chase.

As for Australia, their skipper Mitchell Marsh had limited bowling options to choose from, given that they are playing with only 9 players. They were put under the pump early as first Johnson Charles and then Nicholas Pooran took them apart. After Adam Zampa put an end to Pooran's onslaught, Australia were able to bring the scoring rate down to some extent in the middle phase. Zampa then went on to get rid of Charles before being taken to the cleaners in his final over. While Nathan Ellis was tough to get away in his third over, Josh Hazlewood could not back it up at his end which meant that the Aussies could not stop West Indies from crossing 250. Tim David and Nathan Ellis bowled well in patches for Australia on what was a tough day at the office for the bowling unit.

West Indies get the desired finishing kick and they end up with 257 on the board! After being put into bat, West Indies were off to a rollicking start. Johnson Charles made his intentions clear straight away, as did Nicholas Pooran. After setting the tone, Charles took the backseat in the partnership and watched Pooran unleash a real assault on the Aussie bowlers. The southpaw soon brought up a 16-ball fifty. After Pooran fell on 75, Rovman Powell took over and ensured that the West Indies innings did not lose steam. Sherfane Rutherford picked up where his skipper left off and produced an absolute carnage. His quickfire 47-run cameo of just 18 balls propelled West Indies to 257.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin! The two openers for West Indies are Shai Hope and Johnson Charles. Tim David will be initiating the proceedings with the new ball. Here we go...

The skipper of the West Indies, Rovman Powell says that they wanted to bat first. Adds that they want to bat as a unit and will look to play the whole 20 overs. Shares that the preparation has been good.

Mitchell Marsh, the skipper of Australia says that they will bowl first. Informs that they will be playing with 9 players. Mentions that it is a good opportunity to play West Indies at home in front of the fans.

Australia - Adam Zampa, Ashton Agar, Cameron Green, David Warner, Glenn Maxwell, Josh Hazlewood, Josh Inglis, Marcus Stoinis, Matthew Wade, Mitchell Marsh, Mitchell Starc, Nathan Ellis, Pat Cummins, Tim David, Travis Head.

West Indies - Brandon King, Johnson Charles, Shimron Hetmyer, Shai Hope, Nicholas Pooran, Sherfane Rutherford, Roston Chase, Andre Russell, Rovman Powell, Shamar Joseph, Romario Shepherd, Obed McCoy, Gudakesh Motie, Alzarri Joseph, Akeal Hosein.
TOSS - Australia have won the flip of the coin and they have opted to BOWL first.

Australia, on the other hand, have already played a warm-up match, defeating Namibia despite fielding support staff due to a short squad. David Warner’s explosive fifty was a highlight, and captain Mitchell Marsh made a successful return from injury. With Travis Head, who was exceptional in India recently, Cameron Green, Tim David, and Matthew Wade, their batting lineup is formidable. Pat Cummins, who guided Hyderabad to the Indian T20 League finals, will be key with both ball and bat. His leadership and experience are invaluable. Mitchell Starc, fresh off winning the Indian T20 League with Kolkata, was outstanding in the knockout stages, earning Man of the Match in the final. Marcus Stoinis and Glenn Maxwell have been somewhat inconsistent and will aim to find their form before the group stages begin. Ashton Agar and Adam Zampa will be their main spinners, and they are expected to thrive in these conditions. While the outcomes of these warm-up matches might not hold great significance, both teams will aim to be competitive and build momentum heading into the main tournament. The toss coming up in a bit.

Batters like Brandon King and Johnson Charles were in superb form for the West Indies during that series, while Nicholas Pooran, Andre Russell, and Shai Hope had solid seasons in the Indian T20 League but will be looking to eliminate any lingering rust. Interestingly, their spin attack appears particularly potent this time, with Gudakesh Motie and Akeal Hosein leading the charge, while Roston Chase and Romario Shepherd will be pivotal with their all-round skills. They need more consistency from their pace attack, with Alzarri Joseph and Shamar Joseph bringing fiery speed and Obed McCoy and Russell providing effective variations in these conditions.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks! The ICC T20 World Cup 2024 is just around the corner, and teams are seizing the opportunity to fine-tune their strategies in the warm-up games. The hosts, the West Indies, are brimming with confidence after a clean sweep against South Africa in their recent T20I series and now face Australia in a warm-up match.
